name: Multi Commodity Exchange of India Ltd
title: Multi Commodity Exchange of India Ltd - 534091 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Exchange volumes ran hot in FY26 (ADT ~2.5x, revenue more than doubled to INR2,302 crores), but management gave no numeric guidance, declined April-May participation data and flagged cyclicality and rising expenses.

triggers.label: FY26 ADT ~2.5x, revenue doubled
triggers.quote: supported by nearly 2.5 times increase in the average daily turnover across both futures and options

triggers.label: Equity exchange entering commodities
triggers.quote: as equity Exchanges enter into the commodity space, there could be some natural sort of synergies they have there

red_flags.quote: the product license fees and other expenses line items grew faster than the revenue

summary.headline: MCX FY26 consolidated revenue more than doubled to INR2,302 crore and PAT crossed INR1,300 crore, with ADT up ~2.5x.
summary.overview: Management described FY26 as a very strong year, with consolidated revenue from operations more than doubling to INR2,302 crore and EBITDA of INR1,774 crore. Average daily turnover across futures and options rose about 2.5 times, with bullion growing more than 4 times and energy growing strongly off a high base. Management said growth was both structural and cyclical, but declined to comment on April and May participation and said not every quarter will be a big jump over the prior quarter. Cost lines (product licence fees, other expenses, SGF contribution, software support) rose faster than revenue in Q4, and management said the focus is on efficiency rather than spending less.

financial_highlights.metric: Average daily turnover, futures and options (FY26)
Interest income on margin money (Q4 FY26)
financial_highlights.change: vs INR22 crore in Q4 FY25

financial_highlights.value: About 2% to 3% overall; double-digit share within energy

segments.name: Bullion
segments.commentary: Management said bullion grew more than 4 times and is one of two main volume drivers; market share was stated as unchanged over the last two years despite competitor launches.

segments.name: Energy
segments.commentary: Energy growth was described as good and strong over a very high base; FPIs are a significant contributor within energy, at double-digit share.

segments.name: Indices (BULLDEX / METALDEX)
segments.commentary: BULLDEX options drew strong interest in futures, so management is adding index futures alongside options and plans further work on METALDEX this year.

segments.name: Electricity derivatives
segments.commentary: Early stage; about 50 commercial participants onboarded and UCC numbers rising month on month. Revenue not tracked separately.

segments.name: Coal exchange (subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Licence won for a separate coal exchange to operate as a subsidiary; SEBI approval and further regulatory steps are still required, so it is in early stage.

guidance_outlook: Management said it believes the coming year will be a strong year but would not guarantee sequential growth each quarter, citing cyclicality.
Focus over the coming months will be on efficiency rather than cost reduction; investment in technology and people will continue.
Colocation services can be launched at short notice if the regulator permits.
Management expects FPI participation to grow from the current 2% to 3% of overall ADT, with an onboarding pipeline described as strong.
Capital on hand is earmarked for organic and inorganic opportunities, new product segments and ancillary businesses; early-stage strategies were mentioned without detail.
capex_capacity: Product pipeline: management says it is prepared with the next set of products in energy, metals and other segments, with no launch dates given.
Index derivatives: METALDEX to be pursued further this year; index futures to be added alongside BULLDEX options.
Technology and people investments are continuing; no capex figure was disclosed.
Coal exchange is to be set up as a separate subsidiary, not inside MCX; no timeline given.
demand_pricing: Management attributed volume growth to bullion and energy, with bullion growing faster and the two alternating in strength over time.

Retail participation is growing steadily via digital brokers, the consolidated ledger and better user experience; management said it does not expect all equity investors to become commodity investors.
Mutual funds were cited as a future channel for commodity exposure after a regulatory change allowing more flexibility.

Competition: a large competitor has launched multiple bullion and energy products. Management said recent expiry-date changes in energy lead to shallow one-day-a-month activity, which it views as misaligned with global contract structuring.
RBI lending norms for prop traders may affect credit lines for some members across segments; RBI extended the timeline, and the impact was not quantified.
Management declined to comment on April and May participation, saying there is no dramatic cause for concern.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FPI contribution and status of allowing FPIs into gold and silver contracts?
qa_highlights.answer: FPIs contribute about 2% to 3% of overall ADT and are a double-digit share of energy. The consultation paper is still pending; management will await the outcome.

qa_highlights.question: Is the increase in UCC base-driven, and what is driving retail participation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management wants democratic, steady growth rather than aggressive push. Digital brokers, the consolidated ledger and UX improvements are cited; mutual funds and wealth channels are expected to add participation later.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a reason for the Q4 jump in other expenses and the margin shortfall, and are these one-offs?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed there were no one-offs. Costs are for growth, technology and people. Q4 other expenses were attributed to market development and professional charges.

qa_highlights.question: What is the interest income on margin money?
qa_highlights.answer: Q4 FY26 interest income was INR59 crore, up from INR22 crore in Q4 FY25, due to higher cash placed with the subsidiary. The full-year figure was not given.

qa_highlights.question: Is SGF comfortable, and is there a policy on the share of transaction charges?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said SGF is comfortable with a good cushion. No percentage of transaction charges has been published; SGF needs depend on volatility, margins, volume and OI together.

qa_highlights.question: Does interoperability with equity clearing corporations explain why liquidity is not shifting, and how do RBI norms affect BG and FD funding?
qa_highlights.answer: Management disputed the 55% to 60% BG share cited by the analyst and said FDs are the largest portion and fully funded. Interoperability is harder in commodities because products are not identical to equity instruments; the regulator decides.

risks_watch: RBI lending norms for prop traders and member credit lines; the extent of the impact is unquantified.
Competition from a large competitor in bullion and energy, and from equity exchanges entering commodities.
Energy expiry-date changes by competitors and their effect on liquidity.
Pending SEBI consultation on FPI participation in non-cash-settled commodity contracts (gold and silver).
Q4 cost growth ahead of revenue, with no clear guidance on the expense run rate.
Volume dip in April per analyst, which management did not comment on for the current quarter.
summary.management_tone: Confident on FY26 scale and the structural growth story, but cautious on quarterly momentum and evasive on April–May participation, competitor threats and the prop-trader RBI norms. Management declined to answer questions on uncontrollable industry matters and on specific cost one-offs beyond a brief explanation.
key_quotes: It's been a good year with good results, and I'm very pleased to report this, very exceptional year, building strong momentum that we have seen in earlier quarters.
So, we do believe that we will have a strong year. Now will every year -- every quarter be a big jump over the previous quarter, perhaps not.
So, if you are asking whether our focus is going to be on margins in the coming months, our focus will be on efficiency.
From whatever we see, our bullion numbers remain untouched when it comes to market share over the last 2 years.

growth.why: Management called the coming year strong but would not guarantee sequential quarterly growth, citing cyclicality, and gave no numeric revenue guidance; growth backing is demand-led with no specific capacity, orders or launch dates.
